key_insight: LLM-extracted symptoms from colorectal cancer discharge notes grouped into three stable symptom clusters that were linked to mortality and readmission outcomes.
clinical_relevance: This suggests routine EHR text may provide clinically meaningful symptom patterns that help identify colorectal cancer patients at higher risk for poor outcomes.
method: Extracted 46 symptoms from 2,728 discharge notes of 1,507 MIMIC-IV colorectal cancer patients using zero-shot LLMs.
Built patient-level symptom co-occurrence networks with phi correlation and Louvain clustering across multiple sensitivity checks.
Tested cluster burden scores in logistic regression models for in-hospital mortality, 30-day readmission, and 1-year mortality.
evidence_signal: The approach showed reproducibility across models and resampling, with cross-model ARI 0.727 and strong stability in Louvain clustering, and the Systemic cluster predicted mortality while the CRC Disease-Specific cluster predicted readmission.
watch_item: These findings come from retrospective single-database discharge notes, so external validation is needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Large Language Model-derived Symptom Clusters and Patient Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
